paite: Ngai in, na kilawm hi, ka it; ngai in, na kilawm hi; na maituamna liah ah na mitte vahui bang ahi ua; na sam kelhon bang ahi, Gilead tang pang a kualte.
heading: Pasal
english: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.

paite: Na hate mulmet thak belamnu hon bang ahi ua, sil khit phet a hong paitoute; huai ah amaute chiat in phik anei ua, alak ua kuamah aching a-om kei uh.
english: Your teeth are like a newly shorn flock, which have come up from the washing, where every one of them has twins. None is bereaved among them.

paite: Na mukte khau san-au abang ua, na kam akilawm a; na mit laivomte theibuhfai them bang ahi, na maituamna liah ah.
english: Your lips are like scarlet thread. Your mouth is lovely. Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.

paite: Na ngawng David galvan koihna insang kilam bang ahi, lumbem neute sangkhat kikhaina mun, mihat lum in akivan uh.
english: Your neck is like David’s tower built for an armory, on which a thousand shields hang, all the shields of the mighty men.

paite: Na nawite zuktal nou nih phikte abang ua, lili pak lak a tate.
english: Your two breasts are like two fawns that are twins of a roe, which feed among the lilies.

paite: Ni anem a limliap aman mateng murrah tang ah leh, begaw mual ah ka hoh ding.
english: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense.

paite: Na kilawm hi, ka it; nang ah thilnin bangmah a-om kei hi.
english: You are all beautiful, my love. There is no spot in you.

paite: Lebanon a kipan hon zui in, ka mou, Lebanon a pan kei toh, Amana vum a kipan dak in, Shenir leh Hermon vum a kipan, humpinelkaite kua a kipan, gialbemte mual a kipan.
english: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

paite: Ka lungtang na tuahmangta, ka sanggamnu, ka mou; na mitte lak a khat in ka lungtang na tuahmangta hi, na ngawng a khainiang khat in.
english: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride. You have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.

paite: Na itna kilawm na tel e, ka sanggamnu, ka mou! Na itna uain sang in nakpi in ahoihzaw! Na kinuh gim, gimlim chiteng sang in ahoihzaw.
english: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine, the fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of spices!

paite: Na mukte, Aw ka mou, khuaikhak bang in atakkhia a; na lei nuai ah khuaizu leh nawitui a-om; na puansilh gim Lebanon gim ahi.
english: Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

paite: Huan umsuak ka sanggamnu, ka mou; tui nak kihu, tui kivuh.
english: My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.

paite: Na huansung theibuhfai, gah manphate toh ahi; spiknardi sing suan toh henna pak ahi.
english: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits, henna with spikenard plants,

paite: Spiknardi leh pak gimlim, kepbuk leh singnamtui begaw sing tengteng; murrah leh aloe, gimlim pipen teng toh.
english: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,

paite: Huan atuikhuk na hi a, tuihing lui, Lebanon a kipan a lui luangte.
english: a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.

paite: Khanglou in, Aw mallam huih; huan hong in, nang simlam; ka huan tung ah hong nung in, Na gimnamtuite aluankhiak theihna ding in. Ka ngaihnou ahuansung ah hong pai henla, atheigah manphate ne hen aw.
heading: Numei
english: Awake, north wind, and come, you south! Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and taste his precious fruits.
